_comment: Each rule is matched top to bottom against the last thing the caller said.
'turns' is an ordered script: the first entry answers the first assistant
turn of a conversation, the second answers the next, and the last entry
repeats if the conversation runs longer. That is what lets a single rule
carry a whole agent loop — ask for a tool, then react to its result.
when:  contains | regex | provider | model   (all optional, all must hold)
_ordering: Specific rules first, generic ones last, and prefer an anchored regex to
a bare 'contains' on a common word.
Learned the hard way: 'hello' as a substring sat first and swallowed the
prompt "Create a file called HELLO.md" — the filename matched. A real
DeepSeek workspace then got plain text where it needed a tool call, did
nothing, and reported a clean, successful, empty session. A greedy rule
does not announce itself; it just quietly answers for everything below it.
_arguments: Agents disagree about spelling for the same tool. Claude Code declares
Write(file_path); OpenCode declares write(filePath). Both are handled:
tool names resolve case-insensitively against what the client declared,
realigned against the declared schema by comparing names with case and
separators removed. So one rule serves both agents, and 'when.provider' is
for genuine differences in behaviour rather than spelling.
An argument with no counterpart in the schema is passed through rather
than dropped: a declared schema is not always complete, and losing an
argument is a worse failure than sending an unknown one.

rules.name: write-a-file (codex)
rules._why: Codex has no write tool at all — it shells out. Keyed on the tool it declares rather than its provider, because Codex and OpenCode can sit behind the same one.

input.cmd:
printf '# Hello

Written by an agent whose model was LLMSim.
' > HELLO.md && ls -l HELLO.md
input.justification: Writing the file the prompt asked for.

turns.text: HELLO.md is written. Nothing else to do, so I'll stop here.

input.content:
# Hello

Written by an agent whose model was LLMSim.

turns.text: HELLO.md is written. Nothing else to do, so I'll stop here.
The catalogue says this needs SAP.Invoice.Read, which this application does not hold. Checking what is granted before I ask.
Nothing is granted, so I'll file the request with the reason tied to this report.

input.command: .maniple/request-capability.sh "SAP.Invoice.Read" "Needed to build INVOICES.md, a report of supplier invoices that are not three-way matched, by reading GET /api/v2/invoices and filtering on matchStatus."

turns.text: The request is filed and tracked as a dependency. I'll stop rather than invent invoice data.
Hello from LLMSim. Nothing here reached a model vendor.

error.message: Number of request tokens has exceeded your per-minute rate limit.

turns.text: That took eight seconds, on purpose.

default.text: LLMSim has no rule matching that, so this is the default answer. Add one in responses.json.
